note:
**The 1881 round, schedules 154 to 165 - Newcastle Circus, South Road, Park Drive, Clumber Crescent South and Cavendish Road South.** Transcribed by A. Hagues.

**Robert Evans, architect and Justice of the Peace**, at **11 Cavendish Crescent South**, with his son Robert, 15, already an **architect's pupil**, and four daughters - Edith M, Mary, Ethel F and Dorothy. **The record already knew those four daughters as names without a house.** The page says *South Road*; it is the corner house, and A. Hagues places it on Cavendish. The record holds Robert Evans Sr at 11 Cavendish Crescent South in 1891 and 1911, which agrees. See [[robert-evans-architect-on-south-road]].

**Three households are placed on the record's own earlier evidence rather than on the page**, and each source line says so: **Marriott Ogle Tarbotton** to 6 South Road, **John H Brownsword** to Castlethorpe, and **John Watson** to Burton House - though the page puts Burton House on **Maxtoke Road** and the record has it on Newcastle Circus, which adjoins.

**One is deliberately not placed.** Schedule 162 is **James W McCraith**, solicitor, 28, and the page says Clumber Crescent South; the record holds a James William McCraith at **3 South Road** in 1881. Two different streets for one man on one night. Left unfiled until somebody settles it.

**House names the record does not hold**: **Garden House** on Newcastle Circus. And **Cavendish Road South** is a street the record has no properties on at all, though the page gives two households on it - including **Ernest W Enfield, banker, BA Oxon**, whose family name the record already knows.

**Readings that could go either way are flagged in the source line.** Infants are entered as age 0 with the real age kept in the source.
source: 1881 census enumerator's book RG11/3367, Standard Hill and Limits of the Castle of Nottingham, schedules 154 to 165, transcribed by A. Hagues.
